featured_reviews.name: Javed Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Authentic Taste & Quality Since 1986!
If you are looking for pure, high-quality sweets in Malad West, J.K. Sweets is a must-visit. They have been maintaining their legacy since 1986, and the difference in quality is immediately noticeable.
Why I love this place:
Pure Ingredients: They use premium ingredients like Konkani Kaju and Kashmiri Kesar.
Health Conscious: Their sweets contain no Mawa, no milk, and no artificial flavors or colors.
Quality Guarantee: They use Pharma Sugar and even offer a 100% money-back guarantee on their quality.
Consistent Legacy: Having been around for nearly 40 years, they truly understand traditional taste.

featured_reviews.name: Foodsta 717
featured_reviews.review_text:
Malad's J.K. Mewawala serves only vegan sweets, making it a true gem. In Mumbai, they have three outlets; in Daman, they have one. Bring joy to you and your family this Raksha Bandhan by enjoying vegan sweets. Furthermore, they have sweets that are sugar-free. From 1974 to the present, they have served a wide variety of sweets. In addition to sweets, they also serve toffies, farsan, and dry fruits. We were very pleased with the staff's helpfulness and their explanation of each sweet in detail.

We tried:
Kaju Katli
No Added Sugar Mix Sweet
Roasted Badam Pista White Chocolate

The experience of tasting vegan sweets for the first time was enjoyable.

featured_reviews.name: Viren Patel
featured_reviews.review_text:
Worst experience this Diwali specially for Gift package had got for my staff. What was sad was after sale feedback.

Gift boxes had Red ants on box aliveas well as dead so as soon as 1 of my staff reported I asked to throw them but then too thought to preserve 1 box cover as proof a d to share feedback on episode I faced .. It's first time ever since 2012 since I became regular customer f J k sweets Malad. This time I bought it from Mahavir nagar and faced this unpleasant experience.
Instead of understanding issue and bad gifting experience they expect to bring back sweet boxes with Ants 🐜 .. Bad state of affairs.. Atleast understand customer sentiment specially when they are giving gift it's sad to see such non practical feedback.

It's not just about money but atleast value trust of customer who have blind faith in your business.

Whish you wisdom and better sense of understanding.

Good bye J k !

Loved for its authentic taste and premium quality, Kheerkodom is a must-try for anyone who enjoys classic Indian sweets. If you’re looking for a Bengali sweet shop in Malad West, Sweet Bengal is the perfect destination to enjoy handcrafted sweets inspired by the rich culinary heritage of Bengal.

Experience the perfect blend of tradition and richness with premium dry fruit sweets from Sweet Bengal | Malad West, Mumbai. Crafted with high-quality almonds, pistachios, cashews, and authentic ingredients, these beautifully designed treats are ideal for festive celebrations, gifting, or satisfying your sweet cravings. Every bite delivers a delicious balance of flavor, freshness, and luxury that reflects the essence of classic Indian mithai. Elegantly packed and thoughtfully prepared, Sweet Bengal’s dry fruit collection makes every occasion extra special. If you’re looking for the best Indian sweet shop near Mumbai, Sweet Bengal in Malad West is the perfect destination for authentic sweets and unforgettable taste.

Experience the authentic taste of Daab Payesh at Sweet Bengal, a popular mithai destination known for its traditional Bengali desserts. Served in a classic clay pot, this creamy delicacy combines fresh coconut, rich milk, and perfectly balanced sweetness to create a refreshing and indulgent treat. Every spoonful reflects the true flavors of Bengal and the quality Sweet Bengal is loved for. Whether you’re celebrating a special occasion or simply craving a delicious dessert, this signature sweet is a must-try. featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
MM Mithaiwala was once considered one of the go-to snack spots in its prime years — a place people would specially visit for chaat and mithai. Over time, however, it feels like it has settled into being more of a familiar, comforting neighbourhood stop rather than a standout destination. When I visited recently, it felt reliable and comforting, but not particularly memorable.

Recently tried their batata vada, samosa, and a few of the other popular dishes from the menu.

Over the years, MM has been known for its wide variety, and you’ll find almost everything here under one roof. Some popular picks worth trying include:
•	Dahi Kachori – nicely assembled with sweet and spicy chutneys, fairly typical in flavour.
•	Pani Puri & Sev Puri – good hygiene and presentation, classic sweet-tangy balance, but similar to what you’ll get at most good chaat counters across the city.
•	Khaman Dhokla – soft and fresh, mildly sweet as expected.
•	Kachori – flaky outer crust with decent stuffing, best enjoyed warm.
•	Jalebi & Fafda – especially during festive mornings, fresh and satisfying.
•	Assorted Mithai & Dryfruit Sweets – vast range, neatly displayed, standard quality.

The place remains clean and efficient, making it convenient for a quick bite or takeaway. Overall, it’s dependable and comforting, but the flavours feel quite ordinary — something you can easily find at many corners of Mumbai today.

Though it's costly but people who are foodies they will not see the price due to it's exotic taste.

Usually on Sunday's if you are planning to get Faafda & Jalebi for early breakfast, then please plan accordingly and visit early morning by 7:00 am to get it hot and fresh, as the hours passes through, the one have to stand in a long queue but no worries as the Faafda's and Jalebi's are served hot and fresh, so to avoid the long queue, plan accordingly.

As per the rates of the farsan, as a foodie, I don't feel that it's really that tasty.

Rates for sweets and farsan differs on timely basis and seasonal too.

Staffs members are ok and neither helpful.

Overall, it's worth to spend the money if your going for taste only once.
